note: The prose of the W1d truth-run backlog section of _INDEX.md (lib/backlog.ts writes the section; `pnpm matrix:backlog`). Wave ids are never typed in the code that writes the section: a carry names the gap it hangs on (`anchor`), and the wave it sits under is that gap's route. A {placeholder} is filled from the committed data by the derivation the carry's id names in lib/backlog.ts; a placeholder with no value, or a value no placeholder uses, is refused, and so is a carry with no derivation and a derivation with no carry. {sha} and {baseline} are the intro's own.
heading: W1d truth-run backlog (baseline `{sha}`)
intro: Generated by `pnpm matrix:backlog` from the committed baseline and the triage catalogue, and held to them by `tools/matrix/__tests__/w1d-backlog-index.test.ts`: the tables below are data and are never edited by hand. Each wave starts from the ❌ cases of its table and from the audit ids the baseline never drove. The ❌ list is a floor, not the whole backlog (design §8): an audit id in a not-exercised table is owed a scenario by its wave before the wave can call it closed.

`(+N also)` in a cases cell: N further cases, keyed to another gap and counted once there, that also fail one of this gap's checks. The example cases are the first case of each layer the gap has, then the rest in plan order, up to five. `TRIAGE.md` lists every case and `AUDIT-LEDGER.md` the evidence of every id (both in `truth-runs/w1d-baseline/`).

What the ❌ count leaves out, counted from the same three runs. ░ (planned, never driven): {planned}; ruling 65 keeps these as backlog, not as reds, and the count shrinks as the waves add scenario scripts. 🚫 (no organiser path): {noPath}; each is routed to a wave by its own reason and counted in that wave's section. Held red by ruling 70 only inside `judge regression`: {overridden}.
Regenerate (`$OUT` is any empty directory): run the triage command of `truth-runs/w1d-baseline/README.md`, "Reproduce", into `$OUT`, then
A test runs both commands as printed and requires the result to equal this section.

carries.title: SC-P4 and the prompt's trap 2 contradict each other (false premise 20)
carries.text: `W2-scoring-fidelity.md` trap 2 names SC-P4 as the model of a collectable field that loses to the engine: "the declared 3/0 loses to the FIH 2/1 the rulebook adopts (§7.1), so the case is ❌ until fixed". Two other sources say otherwise. The SC-P4 entry of "False premises found" in this file: "FIH 2/1 shoot-out split" is the FIH Pro League rule only; FIH tournament regulations use 3/1/0 with draws standing and no pool shoot-outs, which the product already does by default, and the gap narrows to "no points fields when shoot-outs are switched on". And design §8's row for this wave: "FIH 2/1 is Pro League only". The goals-and-boards rulebook's RB2B-7 recommends seeding 2/1 when shoot-outs are on for a table stage, but that rulebook says "None is a ruling", and no entry of this file's "Owner rulings" signs it. The baseline cannot settle it: the ledger reads SC-P4 `{outcome}`: {evidence} The planner of this wave resolves which oracle the SC-P4 case takes, with the rulebook's sign-off, before the case is written; a case written from the trap alone asserts a split the other two sources call a Pro League rule. This is false premise 20 of the W1d plan, and not W1d's to fix.

carries.title: Owner ruling 70: three cells held red, and the re-baseline that retires the hold
carries.text: Across the three dispatches the cells {cells} flipped between works and red. Every red reads "round 5 paired nobody (SW-H1)", and the cause is the product's `lots` tiebreak (a UUID-hashed draw, by design) exposing P6 (SW-H1: an empty Swiss round reported as success). Ruling 70 (2026-10-05) records the three RED, cause P6, whatever the baseline run showed: the `ruling70` block of `catalogue/baseline.json`, applied by `judge regression`. **The SW-H1 fix must remove that block and `RULING_70_IDS` (`lib/pr-sample.ts`) and re-baseline L3 in the same change** (`W3-swiss.md`, "Output and handoff"). The guards that notice a stale block fire at the re-baseline, not when the fix merges, so a fix merged alone leaves the override live, where it can hide a regression on those three cells only. In this baseline SW-H1 is keyed on {keyed}. {held}

carries.title: Recommendation (the controller's, not an owner ruling): move P6 up
carries.text: Within this wave, take SW-H1 (P6) early: a real Swiss-into-knockout after a withdrawal can strand on an empty round 5 that says it succeeded. This is the controller's recommendation, as owner ruling 70's entry words it; the owner has not ruled on it.

carries.title: The swiss_playoff R4 reason flip: red in all three dispatches, two reasons
carries.text: {cells} are red in all three dispatches with the same failing checks, but the reason flips: {flips}. SW-H1 is `round 5 paired nobody (SW-H1)`; stall is `stage 2: did not complete`, the drawn-game stall. The triage separates the two by reason, so the committed run (dispatch {committed}) keys them to {keyed}. The SW-H1 fix does not turn these cells green: the stall reason stays with the gap that owns it, and a re-baseline that reads the SW-H1 reason on them again moves them back to SW-H1.

carries.title: swiss_playoff R4 cells the committed run keys to this wave
carries.text: The committed run keys these swiss_playoff R4 cells to this wave: {keyed}. Their reason is not stable: it flips between the stall and SW-H1 across the dispatches (the {owner} carry "{flipTitle}" lists the reason per dispatch). Read them there before counting a move in {gaps} as progress or as a regression: a drop here that comes with a matching rise under SW-H1 is the reason flipping, not a fix.

carries.title: ST-G5 pool of one: a product decision, owned here
carries.text: ST-G5's {cases} cases are the same {scenario} field on {sports} sports: {entrants} entrants snaked into {pools} pools leave pool A holding seed 1 alone, with no fixture and so no member. Its table is empty, seed 1 stands in no pool, and stage 1's `/complete` answers {refusal} (the triage rule's note). Whether to refuse such a field with a named reason, or to change what makes an entrant a member of a pool, is a product decision: not W1d's and not a harness question, so it belongs to this gap's wave. This file records no owner ruling on it.

carries.title: Mexicano R4: an intermittent 500 in generation
carries.text: In {flipped} of the {total} `mexicano|<sport>|R4` cells the failing-check set flips across the three dispatches while the state stays red in all three (`dispatch-cuts.json` holds the {flipped} cells as each dispatch recorded them). A cell's failing set shows the re-seat (`I10-americano-seats-each-person-once`, a person seated twice in a round, with `r4-not-seated-later`), the 500 (`generate` answering 500 INTERNAL: `I4-nothing-ends-stuck`, `I8-generate-named`, `life-loop-bounded`), or both together, and which it shows moves between dispatches. The 500 shows in {per} of those {flipped} cells, in dispatches {ns} respectively. The other {others} cells ({otherSports}) keep one shape. So the product's mexicano `generate` answers 500 INTERNAL on some runs of the same plan and a different failure on others: an intermittent 500. The triage keys every shape to {keyed}, so no red is lost, but the state alone cannot tell the shapes apart, and a fix is proven by all of them going quiet over several dispatches, not by one green run.
